t.1.76.2: Then Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, having saluted the sages headed by Vasiṣṭha and seeing his father agitated, spoke.
t.1.76.1: When Rāma had departed, Rāma Dāśarathi, his spirit now calmed, placed the bow together with its arrow into the hand of the immeasurable Varuṇa.
t.1.76.3: Rāma, the son of Jamadagni, has departed; let the fourfold army, protected by you as its lord, now set out facing toward Ayodhyā.
t.1.76.4: Having heard Rāma's words, King Daśaratha embraced his son, the Rāghava, with both arms and kissed him on the head.
t.1.76.5: Hearing that Rāma had gone, the king, delighted and overjoyed, urged on that army and then went swiftly to the city.
t.1.76.7: The king entered the city, which was filled with citizens joyful at the king's entry and uttering auspicious words, and adorned with throngs of people.
t.1.76.6: The lovely city, decked with pennants and banners and resounding with the loud blare of trumpets, its royal highways sprinkled with water, charming and strewn with heaps of scattered flowers.
t.1.76.8: Kausalyā, Sumitrā, and slender-waisted Kaikeyī, along with the other royal women, were engaged in receiving the brides.
t.1.76.10: Adorned with auspicious songs and clad in silken garments, all those women quickly worshipped at the temples of the gods.
t.1.76.9: Then the king's wives received the highly fortunate Sītā and the illustrious Ūrmilā, and also both daughters of Kuśadhvaja.
t.1.76.11: Then all the princesses, having saluted those who were worthy of salutation, rejoiced, all of them delighted, together with their husbands in private.
t.1.76.13: Among them Rāma, exceedingly renowned in the world and of true valour, became the most endowed with virtues, as Svayambhū is among all beings.
t.1.76.12: Married, skilled in weapons, endowed with wealth and surrounded by friends, those bulls among men live in devoted service to their father.
t.1.76.14: Rāma, high-minded and wholly devoted to her, delighted with Sītā for many seasons, ever enshrined within her heart.
t.1.76.15: Sītā was dear to Rāma, for she was the wife his father had chosen for him; and because of her virtue, and the excellence of her beauty as well, his love for her grew ever greater.
t.1.76.16: And in her heart her husband dwelt twice as much; for by the heart one clearly reveals one's heart, even what lies hidden deep within.
t.1.76.18: United with that charming and most beloved daughter of the noblest of kings, Rāma, son of the royal sage, shone exceedingly, like the mighty Viṣṇu, lord of the immortals, united with Śrī.
t.1.76.17: And to him, all the more especially, was Sītā dear, Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, equal to the goddesses in beauty, like Śrī herself in bodily form.
